items.title: Susan Hiller: Bad Dreams
items.venue: KW Institute for Contemporary Art, main hall and ground-floor exhibition spaces
items.times: Exhibition visiting hours not verified. English-language overview tour: November 6, 17:30–18:30; included in exhibition admission, registration on site.

items.title: Festival Pearls: How to Divorce During the War / Skyrybos karo metu
items.times: 19:00; film 108 minutes, followed by Q&A. Original version with English subtitles.
items.why_candidate: A couple’s separation in Vilnius collides with Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and refugee accommodation, connecting private crisis with geopolitical upheaval. Q&A participants are not named.

items.title: Festival Pearls: They Call Me Danka / Danka
items.times: 21:00; film 104 minutes, followed by Q&A. Original version with English subtitles.
items.why_candidate: Socially engaged fiction about a fifteen-year-old forced into adult responsibility within her family. Relevant to gendered care, childhood and survival; a secondary fit behind the documentary and explicitly political selections.

items.title: Herzbergmaschine — documentary trilogy, with Sven Boeck
items.times: 18:00; listed runtime 140 minutes, with director discussion. German version.
items.why_candidate: Connects Gertrud Kolmar’s forced labour and Berlin geography with Hilde Wenzel’s exile diaries and Sabina Wenzel’s recollections in Brazil. Strong documentary fit for archives, exile and Berlin history; director Sven Boeck attends.

items.title: goat (jp) + Camila Nebbia
items.times: Doors 19:00; concert 20:00. End time not stated.
items.why_candidate: goat combines muted instrumental sounds, non-twelve-tone harmonics and persistent minimalist repetition; Nebbia contributes solo saxophone improvisation. Strong experimental and hypnotic listening candidate.

items.title: Ana Roxanne + Clarice
items.times: Doors 19:00; concert 20:00. End time not stated.
items.why_candidate: The strongest ambient match: Roxanne combines minimalism, slowed-down jazz, vocals and synthesizer drones. Clarice, accompanied by Finn Kraft, adds minimalist experimental folk centred on voice, sound and silence.
